name: THE UNDERTAKER'S
note: Room 13, doc 20. ERRATA 23's named exception to the palette proportions: near-monochrome on purpose, and scrubbed rather than dim. Reached from a map drawn in achromatic pencil grey precisely so a bone map into a bone room is not the adjacency 17b forbids -- step 0 caught it before either existed. DOC 26 gives this room ONE working surface, so the coffin that stood on trestles in front of the table is gone: two large pale horizontals where the writing describes one meant a player clicking the nearer of them got the table's line about a coffin. THE COFFINS' USE override is 'Not yet.' and IT HAS NO VARIANT AND MUST NEVER BE GIVEN ONE -- it is the same line in Act III when Thad is arranging his own funeral in this room, and a second version explains the joke. check-fixed-lines fails the build on a variant being added to it. hotspots.name: THE UNDERTAKER
hotspots.note: Doc 27 note 2: he is never named, and THE UNDERTAKER is the whole of it -- the only person in Consolation whose function is entirely sufficient. Doc 27 gives this character a tree and no examine layer. The hotspot is marked stub for the reason the word already means in this repo: the thing exists so the interaction works and its LOOK and LISTEN lines are honestly absent rather than invented. Three characters x two verbs x three variants is eighteen lines nobody has written, and check-examine-lines names them on every run until somebody does.

LOOK_AT.say: One good suit, in three sizes, rented for viewings and returned afterwards. Half the men in Boot Hill were buried in their own clothes and viewed in this.
repeat: Three sizes, on one hanger, and all three have been let out at the waist.
Half the men on Boot Hill were viewed in this and buried in their own clothes.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is rented, and I am not the size.

LOOK_AT.say: Plain, Respectable, and Handsome. The Handsome is four times the Plain and the difference is a handle.
repeat: There is a fourth line, scratched out, that began with the word Gratis.
Nobody has ever asked me which I would want, and I have decided that is a courtesy.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is nailed up, and I would rather not be seen taking it.

LOOK_AT.say: A jar of teeth. He sells them on to the barber, who fits them to the living. Nothing in this establishment is wasted.
repeat: Still there. I have decided to think of it as inventory.
There are more than there were on Tuesday. I am not going to develop this thought.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Obviously nothing. I checked, and I regret it.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. I have satisfied myself and I should like that to be the end of it.

LOOK_AT.say: North light, and a blind half down. He works by it and he does not want watching.
repeat: The glass is clean. Everything in here is clean.
Boot Hill is that way, up the rise. You can see the markers from this window and he has left the blind so you can.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The street, a long way off, and not much of it.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all.

LOOK_AT.say: A saw, a plane, a brace, and a mallet, hung level and clean. This is a carpenter's shop that has specialised.
repeat: The plane has been used this morning. There are shavings and they are pale.
He makes them himself. I had assumed they came from somewhere.
Nothing.
Nothing. He is not working while I am standing here.

overrides.PICK_UP: They are hung level. I am not the man who unhangs them.

LOOK_AT.say: Every burial in Consolation. Eleven pages. Two thousand people have lived here for twelve years and it is eleven pages, which means most of them left.
repeat: Eleven pages in twelve years, in a town of two thousand.
Which means most of them left. I have been telling myself that all morning.
Nothing.
Nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: Coffins, stacked by size. There are a great many in the smallest size, which I have decided to attribute to storage efficiency.
repeat: Stacked by size, and there are a great many in the smallest.
Six months of work, standing ready. He is not expecting a quiet year.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Naturally nothing. I don't know what I expected.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. Naturally nothing.

overrides.OPEN: There is nothing in it. I have checked, which I regret.

LOOK_AT.say: A bench by the door, for those come to arrange things. It has a cushion.
repeat: Somebody put a cushion on a bench in an undertaker's. I would like to know who and I am not going to ask.
It is worn in the middle, which is the opposite of the Registrar's.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is the quietest bench in the territory and it has earned it.

overrides.USE: I have sat down. It is a very good cushion and that is somehow the worst part.

LOOK_AT.say: Scrubbed to the grain. It is the cleanest surface in the territory.
repeat: Scrubbed to the grain, and scrubbed again since.
It is the cleanest surface in the territory and I would rather look at the ceiling.
Nothing.
Nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: The door out. There is no bell, and I understand the decision.
repeat: It opens onto a lane rather than the street. He is not on Main Street and he is not hiding either.
The step is scrubbed. Of course the step is scrubbed.
Nothing.
Nothing.

entrances.note: Doc 20: reached from the map, and doc 26 gives the room a street door back out to it -- it opens onto a lane rather than Main Street.

lightSources.note: The window: north light, and the 33b exemption is DECLARED here rather than inferred from brightness, per the correction to that ruling. The blind is half down and left that way so a visitor can see Boot Hill before he has to say it.
